title: Auditioning for Johnny Ronica's band after high school
summary: Jones auditioned for the arranger Johnny Ronica at Lentz in the early 1950s but could not read well enough; Pat Sullivan was the lead trumpeter.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Yeah, and I tell you, I liked that too. Well back to your neighborhood. You said Johnny Ronica lived out there? Johnny Ronica lived on Canal Street but I didn't know him that well.
I auditioned for his band in the very early 50s, like right after I got out of high school. But I couldn't read well enough to play with his band.

No, but his was an arranged band. Johnny Ronica is a very fine arranger. And he was playing at Lentz when I auditioned for him. I'm trying to think of who was leaving. Pat Sullivan was a trumpet player. And Pat played no jazz. He played no jazz?

But could read anything. And Pat turned out to be an exceptionally fine lead trumpet player. And he needed somebody to play some jazz. But I couldn't read the book. In those days I couldn't read that well. But that's the first I knew him. And I didn't see Johnny Ronica a few times after that until just a couple of years ago I heard him playing again. I'm trying to think of some of the other musicians that lived in the neighborhood. Sharky lived out in Lake Vista. I thought that was a good piece of it.
